literal: It is precisely the season when men of wisdom employ stratagems.
idiomatic: This is precisely the season when men of wisdom put stratagems to use.

literal: Governor Gao of Jinzhou is talented and fierce in spirit, his heroic designs surpassing the age — like a dragon or serpent; how could one borrow cloud and rain from him!
idiomatic: Governor Gao of Jinzhou is talented and fierce in spirit, his heroic designs surpassing the age — he is like a dragon or serpent; how could one borrow cloud and rain from him!

literal: Zhao angrily said: "I and Governor Gao of Jinzhou treat each other with open sincerity — why do you suddenly suspect and obstruct me and speak such words!
idiomatic: Zhao flared with anger: "Governor Gao of Jinzhou and I treat each other with open sincerity — why do you suddenly suspect and obstruct me and speak such words!

literal: " He then placed Shaozong under detention; only after several days was he released.
idiomatic: " He then placed Shaozong under detention; only after several days was he released.

literal: Thereupon he severed the Xianbei troops under his command and assigned them to Gao Huan.
idiomatic: Thereupon he severed the Xianbei troops under his command and assigned them to Gao Huan.

literal: Gao Huan jointly campaigned against Bufan and destroyed him.
idiomatic: Gao Huan jointly campaigned against Bufan and destroyed him.

literal: When Gao Huan raised righteousness at Xindu, Zhao made Shaozong chief administrator, also appointing him mobile-office commissioner, leading troops at Huguan to resist Gao Huan.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised righteousness at Xindu, Zhao made Shaozong chief administrator and mobile-office commissioner, leading troops at Huguan to resist Gao Huan.

literal: After the defeats at Guang'a and Hanling, Zhao beat his breast in self-reproach and said to Shaozong: "Had I heeded your words earlier, how could matters have come to this!"
idiomatic: After the defeats at Guang'a and Hanling, Zhao beat his breast in self-reproach and said to Shaozong: "Had I heeded your words earlier, how could matters have come to this!"

literal: When Zhao was defeated at Hanling, many soldiers fled; Zhao was afraid and intended to slip away in secret.
idiomatic: When Zhao was broken at Hanling, many soldiers fled; Zhao was afraid and intended to slip away in secret.

literal: Shaozong raised banners and sounded horns, gathering loyal followers; once the army's bearing was restored, he and Zhao mounted their horses at an unhurried pace.
idiomatic: Shaozong raised banners and sounded horns, gathering loyal followers; once the army's bearing was restored, he and Zhao mounted their horses at an unhurried pace.

literal: Later Gao Huan marched from Ye to pursue Zhao at Jinyang; Zhao, pressed hard, fled to Chihong Ridge and hanged himself.
idiomatic: Later Gao Huan marched from Ye to pursue Zhao at Jinyang; Zhao, pressed hard, fled to Chihong Ridge and hanged himself.

literal: As Shaozong was traveling and reached Wutu City, he saw Gao Huan pursuing close behind; he then brought Rong's wife and children and Zhao's remaining followers over in submission.
idiomatic: As Shaozong was traveling and reached Wutu City, he saw Gao Huan pursuing close behind; he then brought Rong's wife and children and Zhao's remaining followers over in submission.

literal: Gao Huan still treated him with favor and courtesy; all his offices and ranks remained as before, and he took part in military planning and strategy.
idiomatic: Gao Huan still treated him with favor and courtesy; all his offices and ranks remained as before, and he took part in military planning and strategy.

literal: At the beginning of Tianping, when the capital was moved to Ye and many affairs were not yet settled, Shaozong and Gao Longzhi were ordered jointly to manage the treasury, archives, and related matters.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping, when the capital was moved to Ye and many affairs were not yet settled, Shaozong and Gao Longzhi were ordered jointly to manage the treasury, archives, and related matters.

literal: In the second year, the Yiyang man Li Yansun gathered a crowd in rebellion; Shaozong was made army marshal of the southwestern circuit and, leading Area Commander Kudi Ansheng and others, attacked and broke them.
idiomatic: In the second year, the Yiyang man Li Yansun gathered a crowd in rebellion; Shaozong was made army marshal of the southwestern circuit and, leading Area Commander Kudi Ansheng and others, attacked and broke them.

literal: When the army returned, he served as acting governor of Yang Province; soon he served as acting governor of Qing Province.
idiomatic: When the army returned, he served as acting governor of Yang Province; soon he served as acting governor of Qing Province.

literal: Sun Qian of the chief minister's secretariat, relying on Shaozong, had his elder brother appointed chief clerk of the province; Shaozong would not accept it.
idiomatic: Sun Qian of the chief minister's secretariat, relying on Shaozong, had his elder brother appointed chief clerk of the province; Shaozong would not accept it.

literal: Qian slandered him to Gao Huan, saying: "Murong Shaozong once climbed the walls of Guanggu City and sighed long, telling those close to him, 'A great man ought to recover his ancestral enterprise — is that not so?'
idiomatic: Qian slandered him to Gao Huan, saying: "Murong Shaozong once climbed the walls of Guanggu City and sighed long, telling those close to him, 'A great man ought to recover his ancestral enterprise — is that not so?'

literal: " Because of this he was recalled.
idiomatic: " Because of this he was recalled.

literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang, the Western Wei general Dugu Ruyuan held Luozhou; between Liang and Ying, bandits and raiders rose in force.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanxiang, the Western Wei general Dugu Ruyuan held Luozhou; between Liang and Ying, bandits and raiders rose in force.

literal: Gao Huan ordered Shaozong to lead troops to Wulao and, together with Mobile-Office Commissioner Liu Gui and others, pacify them.
idiomatic: Gao Huan ordered Shaozong to lead troops to Wulao and, together with Mobile-Office Commissioner Liu Gui and others, pacify them.

literal: His rank was advanced to duke, and he was appointed minister of revenue.
idiomatic: His rank was advanced to duke, and he was appointed minister of revenue.

literal: Later he became governor of Jin Province and western-circuit grand commissioner; on returning to court he was transferred to censor-in-chief.
idiomatic: Later he became governor of Jin Province and western-circuit grand commissioner; on returning to court he was transferred to censor-in-chief.

literal: When the Liang man Liu Wuhei invaded Xu Region, Shaozong was ordered to lead troops against him; he inflicted a great defeat and was then appointed governor of Xu Province.
idiomatic: When the Liang man Liu Wuhei invaded Xu Region, Shaozong was ordered to lead troops against him; he inflicted a great defeat and was then appointed governor of Xu Province.

literal: Wuhei gathered his scattered troops and again raided and plundered; Shaozong secretly won over his followers, and within a few months seized Wuhei and killed him.
idiomatic: Wuhei gathered his scattered troops and again raided and plundered; Shaozong secretly won over his followers, and within a few months seized Wuhei and killed him.

literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, Shaozong was appointed southeastern-circuit mobile-office commissioner, additionally given the seal of opening an office, transferred and enfeoffed Duke of Yan Commandery; with Han Gui and others he went to Xiqiu to plan the advance.
idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, Shaozong was appointed southeastern-circuit mobile-office commissioner, additionally given the seal of opening an office, transferred and enfeoffed duke of Yan Commandery; with Han Gui and others he went to Xiqiu to plan the advance.

literal: Emperor Wu of Liang dispatched his elder brother's son, the Zhenyango Marquis Yuanming, and others, leading a hundred thousand men to encamp at Hanshan, coordinating with Hou Jing in pincer fashion and damming the Si River to flood Pengcheng.
idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang dispatched his elder brother's son, the Zhenyango Marquis Yuanming, and others, leading a hundred thousand men to encamp at Hanshan, coordinating with Hou Jing in pincer fashion and damming the Si River to flood Pengcheng.

literal: An edict still appointed Shaozong mobile-office commissioner, directing military affairs in the three Xu and two Yan provinces; with Grand Commander Gao Yue and others he marched out to attack and inflicted a great defeat, capturing Yuanming and his generals and taking their troops prisoner.
idiomatic: An edict still appointed Shaozong mobile-office commissioner, directing military affairs in the three Xu and two Yan provinces; with Grand Commander Gao Yue and others he marched out to attack and inflicted a great defeat, capturing Yuanming and his generals and taking their troops prisoner.

literal: He then turned the army to attack Hou Jing at Woyang.
idiomatic: He then turned the army to attack Hou Jing at Woyang.

literal: At that time Jing's army was very numerous; the generals sent before him were none that he did not hold in contempt.
idiomatic: At that time Jing's army was very numerous; none of the generals sent against him before escaped his contempt.

literal: When he heard that Shaozong and Yue were about to arrive, he showed deep fear and said to his followers: "Yue's troops are elite, and Shaozong is an old commander — we should all be careful with them.
idiomatic: When he heard that Shaozong and Yue were about to arrive, he showed deep fear and said to his followers: "Yue's troops are elite, and Shaozong is an old commander — we should all be careful with them.

literal: " Thereupon he joined battle with Jing; the generals held back in doubt, none willing to go first, but Shaozong waved his troops straight forward and the generals followed; thus they won a great victory and Jing fled in defeat.
idiomatic: " Thereupon he joined battle with Jing; the generals held back in doubt, none willing to go first, but Shaozong waved his troops straight forward and the generals followed; thus they won a great victory and Jing fled in defeat.

literal: When the army returned, he was separately enfeoffed Viscount of Yongle County.
idiomatic: When the army returned, he was separately enfeoffed viscount of Yongle County.

literal: Earlier, near the end of Gao Huan's life, he had charged Gao Cheng: "If Hou Jing rebels, Murong Shaozong should be the one to meet him.
idiomatic: Earlier, near the end of Gao Huan's life, he had charged Gao Cheng: "If Hou Jing rebels, Murong Shaozong should be the one to meet him.

literal: " At this time he indeed established merit.
idiomatic: " At this time he indeed established merit.

literal: Western Wei dispatched its great general Wang Sizheng to enter and hold Ying Province; Shaozong was again made southern-circuit mobile-office commissioner and, with Grand Commandant Gao Yue, Palace Attendant Equal in Rank Liu Feng, and others, led troops to besiege and attack, damming the Wei River to flood the city.
idiomatic: Western Wei dispatched its great general Wang Sizheng to enter and hold Ying Province; Shaozong was again made southern-circuit mobile-office commissioner and, with Grand Commandant Gao Yue, Palace Attendant Equal in Rank Liu Feng, and others, led troops to besiege and attack, damming the Wei River to flood the city.

literal: At that time Shaozong repeatedly had ominous dreams, and his mind was always ill at ease.
idiomatic: At that time Shaozong repeatedly had ominous dreams, and his mind was always ill at ease.

literal: He privately said to those close to him: "From the age of twenty onward I have always had white hair; yesterday my white hair suddenly vanished altogether.
idiomatic: He privately said to those close to him: "From the age of twenty onward I have always had white hair; yesterday my white hair suddenly vanished altogether.

literal: By reason I infer: white hair is suan — is my allotted span at an end?
idiomatic: By reason I infer: suan means 'allotted span' — is my allotted span at an end?

literal: " Before long, he and Feng were at the dam and saw dust rising in the north; they entered a warship and sat together.
idiomatic: " Before long, he and Feng were at the dam and saw dust rising in the north; they entered a warship and sat together.

literal: A violent wind came from the northeast; near and far were dark and obscure; the boat cables snapped, and the drifting ship was borne straight toward the enemy city.
idiomatic: A violent wind came from the northeast; near and far were dark and obscure; the boat cables snapped, and the drifting ship was borne straight toward the enemy city.

literal: Shaozong judged that he could not escape; he threw himself into the water and died, aged forty-nine.
idiomatic: Shaozong judged that he could not escape; he threw himself into the water and died, aged forty-nine.

literal: Officers and soldiers of the three armies all mourned in grief; the court sighed in sorrow.
idiomatic: Officers and soldiers of the three armies all mourned in grief; the court sighed in sorrow.

literal: Posthumously granted bearer of the staff of authority, military affairs in the two Qing, two Yan, Qi, Ji, and Guang provinces, director of the masters of writing, grand commandant, and governor of Qing Province; posthumous title Jinghui.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted bearer of the staff of authority, military affairs in the two Qing, two Yan, Qi, Ji, and Guang provinces, director of the masters of writing, grand commandant, and governor of Qing Province; posthumous title Jinghui.

literal: His eldest son Shisu was appointed attendant cavalry.
idiomatic: His eldest son Shisu was appointed attendant cavalry.

literal: Soon afterward he was executed for plotting rebellion.
idiomatic: Soon afterward he was executed for plotting rebellion.

literal: Because of Shaozong's merit, the court limited punishment to Shisu alone.
idiomatic: Because of Shaozong's merit, the court limited punishment to Shisu alone.

literal: At the beginning of Huangjian, he was given place in the ancestral temple of Gao Cheng.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Huangjian, he was given place in the ancestral temple of Gao Cheng.

literal: Shisu's younger brother Jianzhong inherited Shaozong's title.
idiomatic: Shisu's younger brother Jianzhong inherited Shaozong's title.

literal: At the end of Wuping, he reached palace attendant equal in rank.
idiomatic: At the end of Wuping, he reached palace attendant equal in rank.

literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui, he was great general and area commander of Die Province.
idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era of Sui, he was great general and area commander of Die Province.

literal: Xue Xiuyi
idiomatic: Xue Xiuyi

literal: Xue Xiuyi, styled Gongrang, was a native of Fenyin in Hedong.
idiomatic: Xue Xiuyi, styled Gongrang, was a man of Fenyin in Hedong.

literal: His great-grandfather Shao was Wei minister of the seven armies and grand tutor of the crown prince.
idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shao was Wei minister of the seven armies and grand tutor of the crown prince.

literal: His grandfather Shouren was governor of the two commanderies of Hedong and Hebei, governor of Qin Province, and Duke of Fenyin.
idiomatic: His grandfather Shouren was governor of the two commanderies of Hedong and Hebei, governor of Qin Province, and duke of Fenyin.

literal: His father Baoji was governor of Dingyang.
idiomatic: His father Baoji was governor of Dingyang.

literal: Xiuyi from youth was cunning and chivalrous, lightly spending wealth and valuing spirit; he summoned bold and lawless men, and when men in urgent distress came to him for refuge, he often sheltered them.
idiomatic: Xiuyi from youth was cunning and chivalrous, lightly spending wealth and valuing bold spirit; he summoned bold and lawless men, and when men in urgent distress came to him for refuge, he often sheltered them.

literal: Prince Xianyang of Wei was governor of Si Province and employed him as legal bureau attendant.
idiomatic: Prince Xianyang of Wei was governor of Si Province and employed him as legal bureau attendant.

literal: Prince Beihai of Wei, Yuan Hao, garrisoned Xu Province and brought Xiuyi in as ink bureau adjutant.
idiomatic: Prince Beihai of Wei, Yuan Hao, garrisoned Xu Province and brought Xiuyi in as ink bureau adjutant.

literal: At the end of Zhengguang, when warfare rose throughout the realm, Hao was made general who campaigns west, area commander of Hua, Bin, and Eastern Qin military affairs, additionally left vice director and western-circuit mobile-office commissioner; Xiuyi was made area commander.
idiomatic: At the end of Zhengguang, when warfare rose throughout the realm, Hao was made general who campaigns west, area commander of Hua, Bin, and Eastern Qin military affairs, additionally left vice director and western-circuit mobile-office commissioner; Xiuyi was made area commander.

literal: At that time there was an edict: whoever could recruit three thousand men would be made separate commander.
idiomatic: At that time there was an edict: whoever could recruit three thousand men would be made separate commander.

literal: Thereupon Xiuyi returned to Hedong and passed through the commanderies of Pingyang, Hongnong, and others, gathering more than seven thousand men in all; he was then provisionally made general who pacifies the north and separate commander of the western circuit.
idiomatic: Thereupon Xiuyi returned to Hedong and passed through the commanderies of Pingyang, Hongnong, and others, gathering more than seven thousand men in all; he was then provisionally made general who pacifies the north and separate commander of the western circuit.

literal: Before long, Eastern and Western Xia, Northern and Southern Hua, and Bin Province and others rebelled; Hao advanced to attack them.
idiomatic: Before long, Eastern and Western Xia, Northern and Southern Hua, and Bin Province and others rebelled; Hao advanced to attack them.

literal: Xiuyi led his command and had considerable merit.
idiomatic: Xiuyi led his command and had considerable merit.

literal: The Jiang-Shu bandits Chen Shuangchi and others gathered along the Fen River bend; an edict made Xiuyi grand commander and, with Mobile-Office Commissioner Zhangsun Zhi, jointly attacked them.
idiomatic: The Jiang-Shu bandits Chen Shuangchi and others gathered along the Fen River bend; an edict made Xiuyi grand commander and, with Mobile-Office Commissioner Zhangsun Zhi, jointly attacked them.

literal: Xiuyi, because Shuangchi was a fellow townsman, went lightly to the foot of the fortress and explained advantage and harm; Chi and the others thereupon surrendered.
idiomatic: Xiuyi, because Shuangchi was a fellow townsman, went lightly to the foot of the fortress and explained advantage and harm; Chi and the others thereupon surrendered.

literal: Xiuyi was appointed garrison commander of Longmen.
idiomatic: Xiuyi was appointed garrison commander of Longmen.

literal: Later Xiuyi's clansman Fengxian and others raised disorder and besieged the garrison city.
idiomatic: Later Xiuyi's clansman Fengxian and others raised disorder and besieged the garrison city.

literal: Xiuyi too, because the realm was in turmoil, planned to act on his own authority; he joined Fengxian in gathering a crowd in rebellion and styled himself Great General of the Yellow Axe.
idiomatic: Xiuyi too, because the realm was in turmoil, planned to act on his own authority; he joined Fengxian in gathering a crowd in rebellion and styled himself Great General of the Yellow Axe.

literal: An edict made Area Commander Zong Zheng Zhensun attack him.
idiomatic: An edict made Area Commander Zong Zheng Zhensun attack him.

literal: Before the army arrived, Xiuyi felt shame and regret; he sent his tent officer Sun Huaiyan to submit a memorial explaining himself and begging for a great general to come and reassure him.
idiomatic: Before the army arrived, Xiuyi felt shame and regret; he sent his tent officer Sun Huaiyan to submit a memorial explaining himself and begging for a great general to come and reassure him.

literal: Emperor Xiaoming of Wei dispatched Northwestern Grand Commissioner Hu Yuanji with an edict to instruct and explain; Xiuyi surrendered.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaoming of Wei dispatched Northwestern Grand Commissioner Hu Yuanji with an edict to instruct and explain; Xiuyi surrendered.

literal: Fengxian and others still held the heights and entrenched themselves; Zhangsun Zhi's army was at Hongnong and Zhensun's army at Lingqiao, and neither could advance.
idiomatic: Fengxian and others still held the heights and entrenched themselves; Zhangsun Zhi's army was at Hongnong and Zhensun's army at Lingqiao, and neither could advance.

literal: Xiuyi, with his father's younger brother Shanle and his younger cousin Jiazu and others, each led righteous warriors to create the momentum of attack and capture, and sent Fengxian a letter showing fortune and disaster.
idiomatic: Xiuyi, with his father's younger brother Shanle and his younger cousin Jiazu and others, each led righteous warriors to create the momentum of attack and capture, and sent Fengxian a letter showing fortune and disaster.

literal: Fengxian surrendered; Fengxian was appointed general of soaring dragon, bearer of the staff of authority, garrison commander of Jishan, and Viscount of Xiayang County with a fief of three hundred households.
idiomatic: Fengxian surrendered; Fengxian was appointed general of soaring dragon, bearer of the staff of authority, garrison commander of Jishan, and viscount of Xiayang County with a fief of three hundred households.

literal: Xiuyi was enfeoffed Marquis of Fenyin County with a fief of eight hundred households.
idiomatic: Xiuyi was enfeoffed marquis of Fenyin County with a fief of eight hundred households.

literal: Erzhu Rong, because Xiuyi was bold, lawless, and changeable, had him sent under guard to Jinyang and detained together with Gao Ang and others.
idiomatic: Erzhu Rong, because Xiuyi was bold, lawless, and changeable, had him sent under guard to Jinyang and detained together with Gao Ang and others.

literal: When Rong went to Luoyang, he took Xiuyi and the others with him and placed them in the camel-and-ox office.
idiomatic: When Rong went to Luoyang, he took Xiuyi and the others with him and placed them in the camel-and-ox office.

literal: When Rong died, Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei made Xiuyi grand commander of the four commanderies of Hongnong, Hebei, Hedong, and Zhengping.
idiomatic: When Rong died, Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei made Xiuyi grand commander of the four commanderies of Hongnong, Hebei, Hedong, and Zhengping.

literal: At that time Gao Huan was governor of Jin Province; when he saw Xiuyi he treated him with great generosity.
idiomatic: At that time Gao Huan was governor of Jin Province; when he saw Xiuyi he treated him with great generosity.

literal: When Erzhu Zhao enthroned the Prince of Changguang of Wei, Xiuyi was appointed right general and governor of Shan Province, provisionally made general who pacifies the south.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao enthroned the Prince of Changguang of Wei, Xiuyi was appointed right general and governor of Shan Province, provisionally made general who pacifies the south.

literal: At the beginning of the deposed emperor of Wei, Xiuyi was made bearer of the staff of authority, rear general, and governor of Southern Fen Province.
idiomatic: At the beginning of the deposed emperor of Wei, Xiuyi was made bearer of the staff of authority, rear general, and governor of Southern Fen Province.

literal: When Gao Huan raised righteousness at Xindu and defeated the Four Huns at Hanling, he dispatched a summons to Xiuyi; Xiuyi followed him to Jinyang, and Xiuyi was made acting governor of Bing Province.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised righteousness at Xindu and defeated the Four Huns at Hanling, he dispatched a summons to Xiuyi; Xiuyi followed him to Jinyang, and Xiuyi was made acting governor of Bing Province.

literal: He also followed Gao Huan in pacifying Erzhu Zhao.
idiomatic: He also followed Gao Huan in pacifying Erzhu Zhao.

literal: When Emperor Wu entered the passes, Gao Huan went to meet him at Lintong Pass and made Xiuyi mobile-office commissioner of the Guanxi circuit, crossing the Yellow River from Longmen.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wu entered the passes, Gao Huan went to meet him at Lintong Pass and made Xiuyi mobile-office commissioner of the Guanxi circuit, crossing the Yellow River from Longmen.

literal: Xue Chongli, governor of Northern Hua Province in Western Wei, garrisoned Yangshi Rampart; Xiuyi summoned him by letter, and Chongli led more than ten thousand men in surrender.
idiomatic: Xue Chongli, governor of Northern Hua Province in Western Wei, garrisoned Yangshi Rampart; Xiuyi summoned him by letter, and Chongli led more than ten thousand men in surrender.

literal: When Fan Zihe held Yan Province, Xiuyi followed Grand Marshal Lou Zhao in breaking and pacifying him.
idiomatic: When Fan Zihe held Yan Province, Xiuyi followed Grand Marshal Lou Zhao in breaking and pacifying him.

literal: During Tianping, he was appointed guard general and southern cadre general, concurrently governor of Ji Commandery, and area commander of the five commanderies of Dunqiu, Huaiyang, Eastern, and Liyang.
idiomatic: During Tianping, he was appointed guard general and southern cadre general, concurrently governor of Ji Commandery, and area commander of the five commanderies of Dunqiu, Huaiyang, Eastern, and Liyang.

literal: He was transferred to Eastern Xu Province.
idiomatic: He was transferred to Eastern Xu Province.

literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang, he was appointed palace attendant equal in rank.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanxiang, he was appointed palace attendant equal in rank.

literal: At the Battle of Shaye, he withdrew with the other armies.
idiomatic: At the Battle of Shaye, he withdrew with the other armies.

literal: On return, he served as acting governor of Jin Province.
idiomatic: On return, he served as acting governor of Jin Province.

literal: Zu Ye abandoned the city and fled; Xiuyi pursued to Hongtong, urging Zu Ye to return and hold the city, but Zu Ye would not obey.
idiomatic: Zu Ye abandoned the city and fled; Xiuyi pursued to Hongtong, urging Zu Ye to return and hold the city, but Zu Ye would not obey.

literal: Xiuyi returned and held Jin Province, settling the people and defending firmly.
idiomatic: Xiuyi returned and held Jin Province, settling the people and defending firmly.

literal: Zhangsun Ziyan, palace attendant equal in rank of Western Wei, pressed the city; Xiuyi opened the gate and hid armored troops to await him; Ziyan could not gauge truth and falsehood, and thereupon withdrew.
idiomatic: Zhangsun Ziyan, palace attendant equal in rank of Western Wei, pressed the city; Xiuyi opened the gate and hid armored troops to await him; Ziyan could not gauge truth and falsehood, and thereupon withdrew.

literal: Gao Huan greatly praised him; on the spot he was appointed governor of Jin Province and mobile-office commissioner of Southern Fen, Eastern Yong, and Shan provinces, rewarded with a thousand rolls of silk.
idiomatic: Gao Huan greatly praised him; on the spot he was appointed governor of Jin Province and mobile-office commissioner of Southern Fen, Eastern Yong, and Shan provinces, rewarded with a thousand rolls of silk.

literal: While Xiuyi was in the province, he captured Duan Rongxian, governor of Zhengping appointed by Western Wei.
idiomatic: While Xiuyi was in the province, he captured Duan Rongxian, governor of Zhengping appointed by Western Wei.

literal: He summoned and reduced the Hu chieftain Hu Chuili and other tribes, several thousand mouths in all, and memorialized to establish Wucheng Commandery to settle them.
idiomatic: He summoned and reduced the Hu chieftain Hu Chuili and other tribes, several thousand mouths in all, and memorialized to establish Wucheng Commandery to settle them.

literal: When Gao Zhongmi rebelled, Xiuyi was made southwestern-circuit mobile-office commissioner to create pincer momentum, but he did not go.
idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi rebelled, Xiuyi was made southwestern-circuit mobile-office commissioner to create pincer momentum, but he did not go.

literal: Soon he was appointed governor of Qi Province and, for corrupt acceptance of goods, was dismissed from office.
idiomatic: Soon he was appointed governor of Qi Province and, for corrupt acceptance of goods, was dismissed from office.
